module.cloud_storage.checks: Looks for storage buckets (AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob, DigitalOcean Spaces) referenced by the site or guessed from the domain; a guessed bucket is kept only on a real public listing, and no object is ever read.
module.cloud_storage.fix:
If it belongs to you, remove public access right away, in the provider's console: AWS S3, turn on "Block Public Access" on the bucket and on the account; Google Cloud Storage, remove `allUsers` and `allAuthenticatedUsers` from the bucket permissions and enable public access prevention; Azure Blob, disable anonymous access on the storage account (see the snippet).
DigitalOcean Spaces: restrict file listing in the Space settings. Firebase: close the database read rules (see the snippet).
If the bucket is not yours (a same-name bucket guessed from the domain), change nothing: report it to its owner or to the provider. Check ownership in the provider account or organization.
Assess what was exposed: list the bucket contents (backups, exports, customer documents, configuration files, keys) and review the access logs (S3 server access logs or CloudTrail, Cloud Audit Logs, Azure Storage logs) to see whether strangers downloaded files.
Treat every secret found in the bucket (access keys, passwords, tokens, certificates) as compromised: revoke and renew it. If personal data was accessible, follow the GDPR data breach procedure (notification to the supervisory authority within 72 hours) and inform the people concerned if needed.
Replace public access with controlled access: short-lived presigned URLs, or a CDN in front of a private bucket (for example CloudFront with Origin Access Control). Leave publicly readable only the files that are truly public for the site, in a dedicated bucket, and never store backups there.
Forbid listing even when some objects must stay public: a visitor should only be able to read files whose exact address they know, not the bucket index (remove the public list permission, for example `s3:ListBucket` or the read ACL for `AllUsers`).
Set up monitoring: IAM Access Analyzer for S3 or Security Hub on AWS, Security Command Center on Google, Microsoft Defender for Cloud on Azure, with an alert as soon as a bucket becomes public again.
Check: `curl -s https://example-bucket.s3.amazonaws.com/` must no longer return a `ListBucketResult` but `AccessDenied`; then run the scan again.
module.cloud_storage.fix_snippet:
# AWS CLI
aws s3api put-public-access-block --bucket example-bucket --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true

# gcloud
gcloud storage buckets remove-iam-policy-binding gs://example-bucket --member=allUsers --role=roles/storage.objectViewer
gcloud storage buckets update gs://example-bucket --public-access-prevention

# Azure CLI
az storage account update --name examplestorage --resource-group example-rg --allow-blob-public-access false

# Firebase
{
  "rules": {
    ".read": false,
    ".write": false
  }
}
module.cloud_storage.title: Exposed storage buckets
module.cloud_storage.why: A publicly readable storage bucket can expose backups, documents and personal data. Accessing third-party hosts requires authorization of the target.
